component.name: Aoide for Linux
component.summary: A native music player for Melete

description.p: Aoide for Linux plays the music on your own Melete server. It is a native app, and the companion of the Aoide app for iPhone: playlists and listening history sync between them through the server.

ul.li: Gapless playback, sample-exact for FLAC, ALAC, WAV and AIFF
Crossfade between tracks, with albums left whole
Infinity: when the queue runs low, it keeps going
Local playlists and a listening history of its own
Media keys and the desktop's media controls

description.p: Pages take their colour from the album cover, and the sidebar, player bar and side panel from the song playing (Settings, General, Accent: From the artwork; a fixed colour keeps the old look). A For you shelf on Home with songs recommended from your listening, to play or to ask for (Melete with For You and ListenBrainz on). Home tiles show the song you last picked from an album, with Play next and Play last in their menu. Playlists number their songs, and a smart playlist menu finds its songs again.

Artists show their portrait when the server has one (Melete 0.9.0): round on artist tiles in Artists and Search, and on the artist's page, where a picture from Wikimedia Commons shows who took it and its licence.

Collections saved on Melete's web in the sidebar, with Play and Shuffle. Covers and artist portraits in Ask for it, with each portrait's credit. An artist's page grouped into Albums, Singles and EPs, Live and Compilations. Rediscover Mix and Heavy Rotation sync for every user on a server.

Settings → Account: change your profile picture, your password and two-factor sign-in, and for admins give a user a new password. Heavy Rotation and Rediscover Mix fill again, Replay's lists match the phone's, and a YouTube import finds songs your library has under another artist.
Importing a YouTube playlist from a CSV export: each video's song and artist are read from its title or channel, without the words video sites add, so your server asks for the right song.
Motion covers your server no longer has stop playing in the full player, instead of playing a kept copy for up to a week. The Motion covers switch is gone: an album's own motion cover always plays.

A new full-screen player: a frosted card on the song's blurred cover, beside the synced lyrics, alone or wide, over a still blur or a moving background in the cover's colours. The controls hide while you listen, and the layout is kept. Covers download at the size they're shown, and the colours match the iPhone app's, with Melete 0.5.0.

Playlists can hold songs that aren't in your library yet: importing a playlist saves all of it, asking your server for the missing songs, which wait in the playlist until they arrive. Search's Ask for It can add a song you don't have to any of your playlists.

Motion covers, and the cover filling the full player. Lyrics, translation, pronunciation and search by description now come from your Melete server. Requests follow along live and say more, playlists can ask for their missing songs, smart playlists get mosaic covers, the sidebar shows playlist covers, Discord can show the album's cover, and profile pictures show.
Ask your server for music it doesn't have: look an album, artist or song up from Search and ask for it, then follow it under Requests.

Plays from Melete instead of Jellyfin: sign in again with a password, a two-factor code or Quick Connect. Albums can be favourited, Listen Together plays in step with other devices, and song searches match a song's own title.
No change in what the app does: the code is reorganised and documented, and the audio thread can no longer stop playback on an internal check.

The first release, for testing beside the Electron app: browsing, gapless playback, the queue, sync with the Aoide plugin, Infinity and Discover, synced lyrics with translation by your own LibreTranslate server, the equaliser, media keys and the tray.
